name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
desc: Develops tokamak fusion energy technology using high-temperature superconducting magnets, building the SPARC demonstration device and planning a commercial power plant.
markets: Pre-revenue; builds SPARC in Massachusetts and plans a first power plant in Virginia; no commercial customers yet.
rationale: Technology-showcase fit for a high-profile deep-tech brand, but pre-revenue with no consumer market; sponsorship budget and need are limited.

name: COX Group
desc: Spanish developer and operator of water desalination, solar, green hydrogen and infrastructure projects, with engineering, construction and concession businesses.
markets: Projects in Europe, Africa, the Middle East and Latin America; clients are governments and utilities.
rationale: International project developer active in the Middle East and Africa; B2B hospitality could help government relations, but brand awareness is low.

name: Crescent Energy
desc: US independent oil and gas producer with Eagle Ford, Uinta, Permian and Rockies assets, selling crude oil and gas.
markets: Operations and customers in the United States only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: US-only upstream producer with no consumer brand; F1 offers little marketing return for a commodity seller.

name: Cypress Creek Energy
desc: Independent power producer that develops, finances, builds and operates utility-scale solar and energy storage projects in the United States.
markets: Projects and power buyers in the United States only; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic project developer selling power to utilities; little consumer brand marketing, so weak F1 fit.
changed: Previously named Cypress Creek Renewables

name: Diamondback Energy
desc: Independent oil and natural gas producer focused on the Permian Basin in Texas, selling crude oil, gas and liquids.
markets: Operations in the Permian Basin; product sold to US refiners and marketers; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Large US shale producer with no consumer brand; a commodity seller with little marketing use for F1.

name: Doral Renewables
desc: Developer, owner and operator of utility-scale solar and wind projects in the United States, part of the Doral Group.
markets: US projects selling power to utilities and corporate buyers; parent group has Israeli origins; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic developer of utility-scale projects with little consumer marketing culture; weak F1 fit.

name: DTE Energy
desc: Diversified energy company whose DTE Electric and DTE Gas utilities supply electricity and natural gas to customers in Michigan.
markets: Regulated customers in Michigan; non-utility businesses in the US; no international operations.
rationale: Regulated Michigan utility with captive customers; sponsorship has little commercial rationale beyond local goodwill.

name: Duke Energy
desc: Large US electric utility supplying electricity and natural gas to customers across the Carolinas, Florida, the Midwest and other states.
markets: Regulated customers in six US states; no significant international operations.
rationale: Regulated US utility with captive customers across the Carolinas and Florida; F1 offers little customer-acquisition value.

name: EDF Power Solutions
desc: North American renewables arm of EDF that develops, builds, owns and operates wind, solar and storage projects.
markets: Projects in the United States, Canada and Mexico; part of French EDF Group.
rationale: Subsidiary of a French state utility with growth in North American renewables; limited consumer brand marketing.
changed: Renamed from EDF Renewables North America to EDF Power Solutions in 2022

name: Emera
desc: Canadian energy company owning regulated electric and gas utilities in Nova Scotia, Florida, New Mexico and the Caribbean.
markets: Utilities in Canada, the US and the Caribbean; regulated customers.
rationale: Regulated utility holding with captive customers across North America; F1 offers little commercial return.

name: EnBW
desc: German energy company that generates, trades, transmits and distributes electricity, gas and water, and runs grids and e-mobility charging.
markets: Mainly Germany with offshore wind and trading in other European countries; owned by Baden-Wurttemberg state and municipalities.
rationale: Large European energy brand with EV-charging and consumer retail; German Grand Prix links are possible but not obvious.
parent: State of Baden-Wurttemberg and municipal associations (Germany)

name: Enfinity Global
desc: Renewable energy developer and independent power producer building solar and battery storage projects across several world regions.
markets: Projects in Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia-Pacific; roots in Belgium and Italy.
rationale: Multi-region developer with global ambitions, though a B2B brand; hospitality could suit investor and offtaker relations.

name: Engie
desc: French multinational that generates and sells electricity and natural gas and provides energy services and infrastructure to customers worldwide.
markets: Operations in dozens of countries across Europe, the Americas, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global energy brand with retail and corporate customers in many F1 host markets; strong hospitality and decarbonisation messaging.

name: Entergy Corporation
desc: Integrated electric utility holding company serving customers in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas, and operating nuclear plants.
markets: Regulated customers in four US states; no international operations.
rationale: Regulated US utility with captive customers and limited marketing culture; F1 fit is weak.

name: Eos Energy Enterprises
desc: Designs and manufactures zinc-based battery energy storage systems for utilities and commercial and industrial customers.
markets: Manufacturing in Pennsylvania; customers mainly in the United States with some international projects.
rationale: Energy-storage technology showcase is conceivable, but small, loss-making company with limited marketing budget.

name: Generate Capital
desc: Infrastructure investment and operating company that finances and owns sustainable infrastructure such as solar, storage, EV charging and waste-to-energy.
markets: Assets in the United States and Europe; customers are infrastructure users and developers.
rationale: Capital provider with a B2B brand; F1 hospitality could help investor relations but marketing use is limited.

name: Greenko Group
desc: Indian renewable energy company operating wind, solar, hydro and pumped-storage assets and developing round-the-clock renewable power.
markets: Assets across Indian states, selling to utilities and corporates; some green hydrogen ambitions.
rationale: Large Indian renewables player; India hosts no race, so brand benefit is limited, though growth ambitions exist.

name: Grenergy Renovables
desc: Spanish renewable developer and independent power producer building and operating solar parks, wind farms and battery storage.
markets: Projects in Spain, Chile and other Latin American countries, plus Europe; sells power to utilities.
rationale: Spanish-listed developer with Europe and Latin America footprint; Spanish Grand Prix ties are plausible but B2B only.

name: Hydro One
desc: Ontario's largest electricity transmission and distribution utility, owning and operating high-voltage lines and local distribution networks.
markets: Regulated customers in Ontario only; no international operations or verified expansion plans.
rationale: Regulated provincial utility with captive customers; F1 has little commercial use despite the Canadian Grand Prix.

name: Hydro-Quebec
desc: State-owned Quebec utility that generates mostly hydroelectric power, operates the provincial grid and exports electricity to neighbouring markets.
markets: Customers in Quebec; electricity exports to Ontario, New England and New York.
rationale: Montreal hosts the Canadian Grand Prix; state utility with monopoly customers, so commercial case is weak.

name: IPX Power
desc: Power producer developing and operating renewable generation and energy storage projects, selling electricity to utilities and other buyers.
markets: Based in Oregon; markets inferred as United States only; no verified international activity.
rationale: Small project developer with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship unlikely to suit its scale.

name: Masdar
desc: State-owned renewable energy company developing and operating solar, wind and green hydrogen projects in many countries.
markets: Projects in over 40 countries across Europe, Asia, Africa, the Americas and the Middle East.
rationale: Abu Dhabi state-backed brand with global projects; hosts the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, giving strong hospitality and sustainability messaging.

name: Matrix Renewables
desc: Renewable energy platform developing solar and storage projects in the United States, Spain, Chile, Mexico, Colombia and Peru.
markets: Projects in the US, Spain and Latin America; power sold to utilities under contract.
rationale: Multi-region developer with institutional owners; B2B only, so hospitality is the main use.

name: Nexamp
desc: Developer, owner and operator of distributed solar and battery storage projects, focused on community solar and commercial rooftops.
markets: Projects in the US Northeast and Midwest; customers are subscribers and commercial hosts.
rationale: US-only community solar provider with some consumer subscribers; modest marketing scale for F1.

name: NextEra Energy
desc: US energy company combining regulated utility Florida Power & Light with a large wind, solar and storage generation business.
markets: Utility customers in Florida; generation projects across the US and Canada.
rationale: Largest US renewables operator, but customers are mainly American regulated; F1 hospitality has modest value.

name: NiSource
desc: Regulated US utility holding company delivering natural gas and electricity to customers in Indiana, Ohio and other states.
markets: Regulated customers in several US states; no international operations.
rationale: Regulated domestic utility with captive customers in the Midwest and no F1-relevant marketing need or consumer choice.

name: Ontario Power Generation
desc: Provincially owned Ontario electricity generator operating nuclear stations, large hydroelectric plants and other generation, selling power into the Ontario market.
markets: Generation in Ontario only; some nuclear technology partnerships abroad; owned by the Province of Ontario.
rationale: Government-owned generator with no consumer brand; Canadian Grand Prix sponsorship has little commercial rationale.

name: Origis Energy
desc: Developer and independent power producer of utility-scale solar and battery storage projects, mainly in the United States.
markets: Projects mainly in the United States; some presence in Europe and Latin America.
rationale: B2B developer with no consumer brand; Miami base and US Grand Prix link give limited hospitality value.

name: Peabody Energy
desc: Coal producer mining thermal coal for power utilities and metallurgical coal for steelmakers in the United States and Australia.
markets: Mines in the US and Australia; customers in Asia, Europe and the Americas.
rationale: Coal producer with a sustainability-sensitive image and no consumer brand; weak fit for F1 marketing.

name: Recurrent Energy
desc: Solar and battery storage developer that develops, owns and operates utility-scale projects, owned by Canadian Solar.
markets: Projects in North America, Europe and other regions; parent Canadian Solar has global operations.
rationale: B2B developer within a global solar group; limited consumer brand, so hospitality is the main use.
changed: Relocated headquarters from San Francisco to Austin

name: Rowan Digital Infrastructure
desc: Developer and operator of hyperscale and AI data centre campuses in the United States for cloud and technology tenants.
markets: US data centre campuses for cloud and AI tenants; no verified international activity.
rationale: Data-centre brand with enterprise tenants; F1 technology tie-in is plausible but company is early and US-focused.

name: RTE France
desc: Operator of France's high-voltage electricity transmission network, running about 105,000 kilometres of lines and managing grid balancing.
markets: French grid operator with some European interconnectors; customers are generators, distributors and large industrials.
rationale: Regulated grid monopoly with no consumer brand; sponsorship offers little commercial return.

name: RWE
desc: German energy company generating power from offshore and onshore wind, solar, hydro, gas and batteries, and trading energy.
markets: Operations in Europe, the US and Asia-Pacific, with large offshore wind portfolio.
rationale: Large utility with growing renewables and corporate customers across several F1 markets; B2B hospitality value but little consumer marketing.

name: SB Energy
desc: Renewable energy developer and operator, owned by SoftBank Group, building large solar and battery storage projects in the United States.
markets: Projects mainly in Texas and elsewhere in the US; part of SoftBank Group.
rationale: SoftBank-owned US developer; technology and data-centre power links exist but marketing need is limited.

name: Solaris Energy Infrastructure
desc: Provider of mobile gas-fired power generation and equipment rentals, originally mobile proppant systems for US shale drillers.
markets: Customers are US oil and gas operators and data-centre power buyers.
rationale: Industrial B2B equipment provider with no consumer brand; F1 marketing value is small.
changed: Renamed from Solaris Oilfield Infrastructure

name: Sunrun
desc: Residential solar company installing rooftop solar and home batteries, sold mainly through long-term leases and power purchase agreements.
markets: Homeowner customers in the United States and Puerto Rico only.
rationale: Consumer-facing solar brand with real marketing spend, but US-only; F1 US races could reach homeowners.

name: Zenobe Energy
desc: Developer and operator of grid-scale batteries and electric vehicle fleet charging and battery leasing in the United Kingdom.
industry: battery storage and EV charging operator
markets: Sites and customers in Great Britain; limited verified international plans.
rationale: UK B2B energy storage firm; British Grand Prix and motorsport electrification link possible but small scale.

name: AESC
desc: Maker of lithium-ion battery cells and packs for electric vehicles and energy storage, supplying carmakers from plants in several countries.
markets: Plants in Japan, the US, the UK, China and France; customers include Nissan.
rationale: Battery supplier to carmakers with electrification story; B2B, though technology tie-in with motorsport electrification is plausible.
changed: Founded as Nissan and NEC joint venture; owned by Envision since 2018

name: Microvast
desc: Designs and makes lithium-ion battery cells, modules and packs with fast-charging chemistry for commercial and specialty vehicles.
markets: Plants in the US, China and Germany; customers in commercial vehicles and other markets.
rationale: Fast-charging battery technology suits a technology showcase, but small company with limited marketing budget.

name: Alpha Generation
desc: Independent power producer that owns and operates natural gas-fired power plants selling electricity into wholesale markets.
markets: US power plants selling into wholesale markets; no verified international operations.
rationale: Wholesale power generator with no consumer brand; F1 offers little commercial benefit.

name: Capital Power
desc: Power producer owning natural gas, wind, solar, coal-to-gas and battery assets in Canada and the United States.
markets: Generation in Canada and the US selling into wholesale power markets.
rationale: North American generator with little consumer brand; limited F1 case beyond local goodwill.

name: Darling Ingredients
desc: Converts food waste and animal by-products into ingredients such as fats, proteins and collagen, and produces renewable diesel.
markets: Plants across the Americas, Europe and Asia; Rousselot and Darling brands; renewable diesel through Diamond Green Diesel.
rationale: B2B ingredient and fuels group with global reach; renewable diesel and collagen brands offer some sustainability and hospitality angles.

name: Duke Energy Florida
desc: Regulated electric utility subsidiary of Duke Energy supplying electricity to about two million customers in central and north Florida.
markets: Regulated customers in Florida only; parent operates in several US states.
rationale: Regulated subsidiary with captive customers; no meaningful F1 rationale despite nearby Miami Grand Prix.

name: Enilive
desc: Eni subsidiary combining fuel retail stations, biorefining, biofuels, EV charging, car sharing and lubricants.
markets: Retail stations and biofuels mainly in Italy and Europe; Plenitude charging and biorefineries.
rationale: Consumer fuel and mobility brand within Eni group, a Formula 1 partner; fuels and biofuels tie in with F1 sustainable-fuel agenda.
changed: Created in 2023 within Eni
f1: Subsidiary of Eni, a current Formula 1 partner

name: Octopus Energy Group
desc: UK energy retailer supplying power and gas to households, known for smart tariffs, heat pumps, EV charging and Kraken software.
markets: Retail in the UK, Europe, Japan, the US and Australia; Kraken platform licensed to utilities worldwide.
rationale: Consumer-facing energy brand with technology platform and strong growth; British Grand Prix and electrification messaging fit well.

name: Santos
desc: Australian oil and gas company producing natural gas and LNG in the Cooper Basin, Queensland, Papua New Guinea and Darwin.
markets: Operations in Australia and Papua New Guinea; LNG sold to Asian buyers.
rationale: Australian gas exporter with Asian LNG customers; Australian Grand Prix gives local hospitality, but no consumer brand.

name: Siemens Energy
desc: Energy technology group making gas and steam turbines, grid technology, transformers and electrolysers, with wind turbines through Siemens Gamesa.
markets: Customers include utilities and grid operators across Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Global industrial technology brand with enterprise customers worldwide; strong B2B hospitality and technology showcase value.
changed: Spun off from Siemens in 2020

name: Tabreed
desc: District cooling provider producing and delivering chilled water to commercial, residential and public buildings across the Gulf and India.
markets: Operations in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Qatar and India.
rationale: Gulf infrastructure brand in the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix market; district cooling serves venues and real estate, so B2B hospitality fits.

name: Tata Power
desc: Indian integrated power company generating thermal, hydro, solar and wind electricity, distributing power, and selling rooftop solar and EV charging.
markets: Operations mainly in India, with some overseas generation assets; consumer solar and charging brands.
rationale: Large Indian consumer-facing power brand within Tata group; India has no race, but EV charging marketing is plausible.

name: Terna
desc: Owner and operator of Italy's high-voltage electricity transmission grid, with dispatching, interconnections and storage projects.
markets: Italian grid operator with some interconnectors abroad; customers are electricity producers and distributors.
rationale: Regulated grid operator with no consumer business; Italian Grand Prix gives hospitality but weak commercial rationale.

name: Valero Energy
desc: World's largest independent petroleum refiner, making gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, plus renewable diesel and ethanol.
markets: Refineries in the US, Canada and the UK; fuel sold at wholesale and branded retail stations.
rationale: Large fuel brand with consumer-facing retail; F1 linked to sustainable-fuel narrative, though American focus.

name: XPLR Infrastructure
desc: Owner of contracted wind, solar and battery storage assets and natural gas pipelines, formerly NextEra Energy Partners.
markets: Assets in the United States; sponsored by NextEra Energy; no international operations.
rationale: Yield-focused asset owner with no consumer brand or marketing culture; weak F1 fit.
changed: Renamed from NextEra Energy Partners in 2025

name: AEP Transmission
desc: Electric transmission business of American Electric Power, operating high-voltage lines and substations across several US states.
markets: Regulated transmission in the US Midwest and Mid-Atlantic; no international operations.
rationale: Regulated transmission subsidiary with no consumer brand; sponsorship has no commercial rationale.

name: Solid Power
desc: Develops solid-state battery materials and cells for electric vehicles, including sulfide-based solid electrolytes, with automaker and cell-maker partners.
markets: Partners include BMW, Ford and SK On; customers in the US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Next-generation battery technology showcase; early-stage and small, so budget is limited, though automaker links are relevant.

name: Korea Electric Power
desc: State-controlled South Korean utility owning the national transmission and distribution network and large generation subsidiaries, selling electricity to customers.
markets: Monopoly customers in South Korea; overseas power projects in the Middle East and Asia.
rationale: State-controlled monopoly with no consumer choice over supplier; sponsorship would have weak commercial rationale despite the national brand.

name: Stegra
desc: Builds a large green steel plant in Boden, Sweden, using hydrogen from renewable power to make near-zero-emission steel.
markets: Pre-revenue plant under construction in Sweden; customers are European carmakers and industrial buyers.
rationale: Brand-led sustainability story with automaker customers; but pre-revenue and capital-constrained, limiting sponsorship budget.
changed: Renamed from H2 Green Steel in 2024

name: Fortum
desc: Finnish clean energy company generating hydro, nuclear, wind and solar power, selling electricity and heat, and providing recycling services.
markets: Operations in the Nordic countries, Poland and the Baltics; businesses and consumers.
rationale: Nordic energy brand with consumer retail and recycling; Europe-only footprint limits F1 value.

name: LG Energy Solution
desc: Manufactures lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles, energy storage systems and IT devices, supplying carmakers from plants worldwide.
markets: Plants in Korea, the US, Poland, China and elsewhere; supplies GM, Hyundai, Stellantis and Honda.
rationale: Global battery supplier to carmakers with electrification story; B2B technology showcase and automaker hospitality fit.

name: Aditya Birla Renewables
desc: Renewable energy arm of Aditya Birla Group that develops and operates solar and wind plants supplying industrial and commercial customers.
markets: Plants and customers in India; some operations in Southeast Asia and elsewhere through the group.
rationale: Indian B2B renewables arm of a large conglomerate; little standalone consumer brand.

name: Altus Power
desc: Provider of commercial-scale solar power and energy storage, owning and operating rooftop and ground-mounted solar for commercial and public customers.
markets: Commercial and public-sector solar customers in the United States only; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic B2B solar owner with little brand marketing and a pending ownership change; weak F1 fit overall.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to be acquired by TPG

name: AMEA Power
desc: Renewable energy developer and independent power producer building solar, wind and battery storage projects in Africa and the Middle East.
markets: Projects in Egypt, Morocco, Jordan and other African and Middle Eastern countries; power sold to state utilities.
rationale: Dubai-based developer in the Gulf and Africa; B2B hospitality at Gulf races could suit government and investor relations.

name: Base Power
desc: Sells home battery systems and electricity plans to Texas homeowners, installing batteries without upfront cost and aggregating them as capacity.
markets: Homeowners in Texas only; no verified expansion plans beyond the US.
rationale: Consumer-facing and growing in Texas, where the US Grand Prix is held; limited scale and local focus.

name: BrightNight
desc: Developer of hybrid solar-plus-storage projects selling clean power to utilities and large customers, using its own software platform.
markets: Projects in the United States and India selling power to utilities and large customers.
rationale: B2B developer with limited consumer brand; hospitality may help utility and corporate relationships.

name: Brookfield Renewable Partners
desc: Owner and operator of hydro, wind, solar and storage power assets across North America, South America, Europe and Asia.
markets: Assets in North and South America, Europe and Asia; sells to utilities and corporate buyers.
rationale: Global renewables owner with technology and corporate offtakers; B2B hospitality and sustainability messaging, though little consumer brand.

name: Canadian Solar
desc: Makes solar modules and battery energy storage systems and develops utility-scale solar and storage projects worldwide.
markets: Manufacturing mainly in China and Southeast Asia; sales across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Global solar brand with consumer and utility customers; sponsorship could build brand awareness and hospitality in many markets.

name: Centrus Energy
desc: Supplies nuclear fuel and enrichment services, including low-enriched and high-assay uranium for reactors, working with the US Department of Energy.
markets: Customers are nuclear utilities in the US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Nuclear fuel supplier with B2B utility customers and no consumer brand; F1 fit is weak.

name: Drax Group
desc: UK renewable power company generating electricity from biomass at Drax Power Station in Yorkshire, plus hydro, pumped storage and supply.
markets: UK power generation; biomass pellet production in the US and Canada; customers in the UK and Europe.
rationale: UK power brand tied to biomass debate; British Grand Prix hospitality is possible but reputational risk limits fit.

name: Edify Energy
desc: Developer that develops, finances and operates utility-scale solar farms and battery storage projects in Australia.
markets: Projects in Australia; power sold to utilities and corporate buyers.
rationale: Australian project developer with little consumer marketing; Australian Grand Prix could give local hospitality but weak overall fit.

name: Elia
desc: Belgian electricity transmission system operator running the national high-voltage grid, part of Elia Group which also owns Germany's 50Hertz.
markets: Operates grids in Belgium and, through the group, Germany; customers are generators and distributors.
rationale: Regulated grid operator with no consumer brand; sponsorship has little commercial rationale despite the Belgian Grand Prix heritage.

name: EnergyRe
desc: Clean energy company based in New York, described by Crunchbase as being at the centre of the clean energy future.
markets: Based in New York; activities and markets are not confirmed.
rationale: Little information on its business; fit with F1 cannot be judged and appears weak.

name: Evergy
desc: Electric utility serving about 1.7 million customers in Kansas and Missouri, generating power from nuclear, coal, gas, wind and solar.
markets: Regulated customers in Kansas and Missouri only; no international operations or verified expansion plans.
rationale: Regulated Midwest utility with captive customers and little marketing culture; F1 offers little commercial return to it.

name: Fervo Energy
desc: Develops enhanced geothermal power using horizontal drilling to produce round-the-clock clean electricity, with its Cape Station project in Utah.
markets: Projects in the western United States selling power to utilities and technology buyers.
rationale: Technology showcase for clean firm power and Texas base, but early commercial stage and limited marketing budget.

name: Fidra Energy
desc: Developer of large-scale battery energy storage, including the Thorpe Marsh project in Yorkshire, one of Europe's largest.
markets: Projects in Great Britain; revenue from grid services and energy trading.
rationale: UK grid-battery developer with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit despite British Grand Prix proximity.

name: Form Energy
desc: Develops iron-air batteries that store electricity for about 100 hours at low cost for utilities, with a West Virginia factory.
markets: Factory in West Virginia; pilot projects with US utilities; no verified international sales.
rationale: Technology showcase potential, but early commercial stage with limited marketing budget and a B2B utility audience.

name: GE Vernova
desc: Energy equipment company making gas turbines, wind turbines, grid equipment and electrification software, and servicing power plants worldwide.
markets: Customers are utilities and industrials in North America, Europe, Asia and the Middle East; spun off in 2024.
rationale: Global industrial technology brand with enterprise customers and decarbonisation story; strong B2B hospitality and technology showcase value.
changed: Spun out of General Electric in 2024

name: Gibson Energy
desc: Canadian midstream company that stores, gathers, processes and markets crude oil and refined products, with terminals at Hardisty and Edmonton.
markets: Operations in Canada and the US; customers are oil producers and refiners.
rationale: B2B midstream operator with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship has little commercial rationale.

name: GoodLeap
desc: Provides point-of-sale financing and software for home solar panels, batteries, roofing, HVAC and other home improvement projects.
markets: Installers and homeowners in the United States only.
rationale: US fintech with installer and consumer channels; brand reach is domestic, giving moderate marketing use at US races.

name: Greenbacker Group
desc: Develops, owns and manages solar, wind and storage assets and runs an investment management business with funds for investors.
markets: Assets and investors mainly in the United States.
rationale: Asset-owner and fund manager with investor audience; F1 hospitality could help investors but marketing culture is limited.

name: Hydrostor
desc: Develops advanced compressed air energy storage in underground caverns for utilities, offering storage of eight hours or more.
markets: Projects in Australia, California and Canada; customers are utilities and grid operators.
rationale: Technology developer with utility customers and no consumer brand; Australian and Canadian races give limited hospitality.

name: Juniper Green Energy
desc: Indian renewable energy developer and independent power producer building and operating wind, solar and hybrid projects and green hydrogen plans.
markets: Projects and customers in India; no verified international operations.
rationale: Indian B2B developer with little consumer brand; no race in India and weak fit.

name: Jupiter Power
desc: Independent power producer building and operating standalone battery storage projects, selling grid services and energy mainly in Texas and California.
markets: Projects in ERCOT in Texas and in California.
rationale: B2B battery operator with no consumer brand; Austin base and US Grand Prix give limited hospitality value.

name: Meja Urja Nigam
desc: Coal-fired power company operating the Meja station near Prayagraj, a joint venture of NTPC and the Uttar Pradesh state generator.
markets: Single power station in Uttar Pradesh selling electricity to state distributors.
rationale: Single-site state joint-venture generator with no brand marketing; F1 has no rationale.

name: Noor Energy 1
desc: Owner of the 950-megawatt Noor Energy 1 concentrated solar and photovoltaic project at the Mohammed bin Rashid solar park.
markets: Single project in Dubai, selling power to Dubai Electricity and Water Authority.
rationale: Single-asset project vehicle with no marketing function or consumer brand; F1 sponsorship is not relevant to it.

name: NuScale Power
desc: Develops small modular nuclear reactors, spun out of Oregon State University, earning revenue from design and licensing for utilities.
markets: Prospective customers in the US, Europe and Asia; projects with utilities and industrial partners.
rationale: Technology developer with limited commercial revenue; B2B audience makes F1 weak but a technology showcase is conceivable.

name: Orano
desc: French nuclear fuel cycle company that mines and enriches uranium and recycles used fuel for nuclear utilities worldwide.
markets: Customers are nuclear utilities in Europe, Asia and North America; mines in Niger, Kazakhstan and Canada.
rationale: State-owned industrial B2B brand with global utility customers; F1 sponsorship unlikely and image-sensitive.

name: Palmetto
desc: Clean energy software and financing company selling residential solar and energy products through platforms and installer partners.
markets: Homeowners and installers in the United States only.
rationale: US clean-energy fintech with consumer and installer reach; modest marketing scale and domestic focus.

name: PPL
desc: Electric utility holding company supplying electricity and natural gas to about 3.6 million customers in Pennsylvania, Kentucky and Rhode Island.
markets: Regulated electricity and gas customers in Pennsylvania, Kentucky and Rhode Island only; no international operations.
rationale: Regulated domestic utility with captive customers and no marketing need; F1 sponsorship has no real commercial rationale.

name: Primergy Solar
desc: Solar and storage developer building utility-scale projects in the United States, a unit of Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners.
markets: Projects in the western United States selling to utilities and corporate buyers.
rationale: B2B developer owned by an infrastructure investor; little brand marketing, so weak F1 fit.

name: Raizen
desc: Brazilian sugar, ethanol and fuel group distributing fuels under the Shell licence at more than 8,000 service stations in Brazil.
markets: Operations in Brazil, with sugar and ethanol exports and some activity in Argentina and Paraguay.
rationale: Large consumer fuel brand in Brazil, host of a Grand Prix; Shell licence and ethanol fit F1 fuels narrative.
f1: Joint venture of Cosan and Shell, Shell-branded stations under licence; Shell is a current F1 partner

name: REC Limited
desc: Indian state-owned non-banking finance company lending to power, renewable energy and infrastructure projects across India.
markets: Lends to state utilities and infrastructure developers in India only.
rationale: State-owned lender with institutional borrowers and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.
changed: Formerly Rural Electrification Corporation

name: Redaptive
desc: Energy-as-a-service provider that funds, installs and operates efficiency upgrades such as lighting, HVAC and controls for commercial customers.
markets: Commercial customers in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: B2B service provider with enterprise customers; F1 hospitality could help sales, but marketing scale is modest.

name: rPlus Energies
desc: Developer building utility-scale solar and storage plants in the western United States, including Utah, to replace coal plant capacity.
markets: Projects in Utah and the western United States; customers are utilities.
rationale: Domestic B2B developer selling power to western US utilities with little brand marketing; weak F1 fit overall.

name: Sabesp
desc: Water and sewage utility serving about 28 million people across 375 municipalities in Sao Paulo state, privatised in 2024.
markets: Regulated water and sewage customers in Sao Paulo state only; no international operations.
rationale: Regulated water monopoly in Brazil; Sao Paulo hosts a Grand Prix but commercial rationale is weak.
changed: Privatised in 2024 with Equatorial as reference shareholder

name: Serentica Renewables
desc: Renewable energy platform developing hybrid solar, wind and storage projects supplying round-the-clock clean power to large industrial customers.
markets: Industrial customers in India only; backed by KKR; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Indian B2B developer with industrial buyers; no race in India and little brand marketing.

name: Silicon Ranch
desc: Developer and operator of utility-scale solar farms and agrivoltaic projects in the United States, selling electricity to utilities and corporates.
markets: Over 100 solar farms in the United States; customers are utilities and corporates.
rationale: B2B solar owner with farming-linked brand; Shell ownership brings a link to an F1 partner but own marketing is modest.
f1: Majority owned by Shell, a current Formula 1 partner

name: Skyborn Renewables
desc: Developer of offshore and onshore wind and solar projects that develops, builds and operates renewable generation, based in Hamburg.
markets: Hamburg-based developer; project countries inferred as Europe and other regions, not confirmed.
rationale: B2B wind developer with little consumer brand; F1 hospitality could aid investor and partner relations only.
changed: Renamed Skyborn Renewables

name: SLB
desc: Oilfield services and technology company providing reservoir characterisation, drilling, completion, production and digital services to energy producers worldwide.
markets: Operates in over 100 countries serving oil and gas companies on every continent.
rationale: Global industrial technology brand with enterprise customers; strong B2B hospitality and technology showcase value in many F1 host countries.
changed: Renamed from Schlumberger to SLB in 2022

name: Solar Landscape
desc: Community solar developer installing solar panels on commercial and warehouse rooftops and selling clean power to local households and businesses.
markets: Projects in New Jersey and other US states; no international operations.
rationale: Local rooftop solar developer with limited marketing scale and no international markets; weak F1 fit overall.

name: Southern Water
desc: Water and wastewater utility serving about 4.7 million customers in Kent, Sussex, Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.
markets: Regulated water customers in southern England only; no international operations or verified expansion plans.
rationale: Regulated water monopoly with reputational issues over sewage; sponsorship has weak commercial rationale.

name: Swift Current Energy
desc: Developer and owner of utility-scale solar, wind and battery storage projects in the US, selling power to utilities and corporates.
markets: Projects and customers in the United States only; no verified international activity or expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic B2B developer with little consumer brand or marketing culture; weak F1 fit overall.

name: T1 Energy
desc: Manufacturer of solar modules and cells in the United States, formerly FREYR Battery and linked to Trina Solar.
markets: Texas module plant selling to US project developers; previously a battery developer.
rationale: Domestic manufacturer with B2B customers; Austin base and US Grand Prix provide limited hospitality value.

name: Talos Energy
desc: Independent oil and gas producer focused on US Gulf of Mexico offshore production, with some operations in Mexico.
markets: Offshore operations in the US Gulf of Mexico and Mexico; sells to refiners and marketers.
rationale: Offshore producer with no consumer brand; Mexican and US races provide little commercial benefit.

name: TXNM Energy
desc: Utility holding company, formerly PNM Resources, owning PNM in New Mexico and TNMP in Texas and serving about 800,000 customers.
markets: Regulated customers in New Mexico and Texas only.
rationale: Regulated domestic utility with captive customers in New Mexico and Texas; no F1 rationale at all.

name: UGI
desc: Energy distribution holding company owning AmeriGas, the largest US propane retailer, UGI Utilities for gas and electricity, and UGI International.

name: Voltalia

markets: Assets in Brazil, France, Egypt and other countries; services business and corporate power buyers.

name: X-energy
desc: Designs the Xe-100 high-temperature gas-cooled small modular reactor and TRISO-X fuel, backed by Amazon and Dow.
markets: Pre-revenue; planned US projects with Dow and Amazon.

name: Zelestra
desc: Spanish renewable developer, formerly Solarpack and owned by EQT, building and operating solar, wind and storage projects in Europe.
markets: Projects in Spain, Italy, Germany, Chile, the US and other countries.

name: Klabin

name: Axpo

rationale: Regional energy brand with corporate customers; Europe-focused B2B hospitality value but no consumer marketing.

name: Orsted
desc: Danish renewable energy company and the world's largest offshore wind developer, formerly the oil and gas firm DONG Energy.
markets: Offshore wind farms in Europe, the US and Asia-Pacific selling power to utilities and corporates.

name: PG&E
desc: Utility providing electricity and natural gas to about 16 million people across northern and central California.

name: AEP Texas
desc: Regulated electric transmission and distribution utility serving about one million customers in south and west Texas, owned by AEP.
markets: Regulated delivery service in south and west Texas only.
rationale: Regulated subsidiary delivering power for retailers; no consumer brand and no F1 rationale.

name: Alpiq Energia Italia
desc: Italian arm of Swiss energy group Alpiq producing and trading electricity and gas and selling energy services to industrial customers.
markets: Industrial and commercial customers in Italy; gas-fired and renewable plants.
rationale: B2B energy supplier with no consumer brand; Italian races give limited hospitality value.

name: Climate United
desc: Non-profit climate finance coalition funding clean energy and climate projects with a federal award from the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund.
markets: Operates in the United States only; funds projects through partner lenders.
rationale: Non-profit financing vehicle with no commercial brand to market; sponsorship would be inappropriate and a very poor F1 fit.

name: Coalition for Green Capital
desc: Non-profit that helped create state green banks and received a federal Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund award for clean energy financing.
markets: Operates in the United States with state and local governments and lenders.
rationale: Non-profit with no commercial brand to market; sponsorship would be inappropriate and a very poor F1 fit.

name: Enlight Renewable Energy
desc: Developer and owner of solar, wind and storage projects in Israel, the US and Europe, selling power to utilities.
markets: Projects in Israel, the US and Europe under long-term contracts.
rationale: Listed B2B developer with transatlantic growth; hospitality could help investor relations, but little consumer brand.

name: FirstEnergy
desc: Electric utility holding company serving about six million customers in Ohio, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, West Virginia, Maryland and New York.
markets: Regulated customers in Ohio, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, West Virginia, Maryland and New York only; no international operations.

name: Intersect Power
desc: Developer of utility-scale solar, battery storage and co-located power and data centre campuses for large technology and industrial buyers.

name: Oglethorpe Power
desc: Georgia electric membership cooperative generating and supplying wholesale power to 38 member cooperatives, including a share of Plant Vogtle.

name: Round-the-Clock renewable ...
desc: Renewable energy project recorded by Crunchbase as a hybrid power project supplying electricity around the clock.
